stem: A trigger must change a field on the record being saved without extra DML. Which event?
explanation: Before triggers can change Trigger.new directly and the values are saved without DML.

stem: Which trigger type is needed to read the Id of a newly inserted record?
explanation: Ids are assigned when the record is saved, so they exist in after triggers.

stem: Which context variable is NOT available in a before insert trigger?
explanation: newMap needs Ids, which do not exist before insert.

stem: Which context variable is available in a delete trigger?
explanation: On delete there is no new version of the record, so Trigger.new is not available. Use Trigger.old or Trigger.oldMap to read the records being deleted.

stem: Which events exist for undelete?
explanation: Salesforce offers only an after undelete event, because the record needs its Id restored first. Before and after exist for insert, update and delete.

stem: What can a developer do with Trigger.new in an after trigger?

options.text: Change field values and have them saved

explanation: Records in after triggers are read-only.

stem: Which method blocks a save from a trigger and shows a message?
explanation: addError on a record or field prevents saving and displays the message.

stem: How many records can a trigger receive in one invocation, at most, in a normal save?
explanation: Triggers process batches of up to 200 records.

stem: Which is the best practice for triggers per object?

options.text: One trigger per object with logic in a handler class
As many triggers as needed with logic inline

explanation: One trigger per object gives predictable order and keeps logic testable.

stem: Which comes first in the order of execution?
explanation: Before-save flows run first, then before triggers.

stem: Which sequence is correct?

options.text: Before trigger, validation rules, after trigger, commit
Validation rules, before trigger, after trigger, commit
After trigger, before trigger, validation rules, commit

explanation: Before triggers run, then system and custom validation, then the save, then after triggers, then commit.

stem: An error occurs in an after trigger. What happens to the transaction?

options.text: Only the trigger's changes are rolled back
The record is saved and a task is created

explanation: Uncaught errors roll back the whole transaction.

stem: Where do after-save record-triggered flows run relative to after triggers?
explanation: After-save flows run after after triggers and before the commit.

stem: How can a trigger avoid infinite recursion?

options.text: Use a static Boolean or only act when a field really changed

explanation: Static variables persist for the transaction and can guard against repeated runs.

stem: How can a trigger tell that Status__c changed on update?

options.text: Compare Trigger.oldMap.get(Id).Status__c with the new value

explanation: Compare new and old values through oldMap.

stem: A trigger works for one record in the UI but fails during a data load of 200 records. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: SOQL or DML inside a loop

explanation: Non-bulk-safe code hits governor limits at scale.

stem: Which statement is correct about validation rules and before triggers?

options.text: A before trigger runs before custom validation rules
Validation rules run before before triggers
They run at the same time

explanation: Before triggers run before custom validation rules, so they can fix data first.

stem: When is a flow usually a better choice than a trigger?
explanation: Prefer declarative tools for simple automation.

stem: Which TWO belong in a trigger handler pattern? (Choose 2)

options.text: The trigger only calls the handler
Business logic is in a handler class that is easier to test
SOQL queries are placed inside the trigger loop
Every event has a separate trigger

explanation: Keep the trigger thin and put testable logic in a handler.

stem: Which context variable tells you the type of operation as an enum in a trigger?
explanation: Trigger.operationType returns a System.TriggerOperation value.

options.text: The load fails with a limit error after the 100th query
It succeeds because the trigger is a before trigger
It succeeds but only 100 contacts are saved
Salesforce splits the load into 200 queries automatically

explanation: Each loop pass runs a query, so 200 records need 200 queries. The synchronous limit is 100, and the uncatchable limit exception rolls the whole load back. The fix is one query on a Set of AccountIds.

options.text: Fills a blank planned date on each new record with no DML statement
Inserts a second installation for each blank date
Fails because Trigger.new cannot be changed
Updates the date only after the record is committed

explanation: In a before trigger the records are not saved yet, so changing Trigger.new fields is saved automatically and needs no update statement.

options.text: A runtime error, because records in after triggers are read-only
The description is saved only for the first record

explanation: Trigger.new is read-only in after triggers. To change the same records you must use a before trigger, or query and update separate copies, which risks recursion.

stem: A trigger on Opportunity must act only when Stage actually changes. Which condition is correct inside an after update loop?
explanation: oldMap holds the previous values by Id, so comparing the old and new StageName detects a real change.

stem: An after update trigger updates the same object, which fires the trigger again. Which design prevents the second run?

options.text: A static Boolean in a handler class that is set after the first run
A global Boolean in the trigger body

explanation: Static variables keep their value for the whole transaction, so a flag set on the first pass can stop repeat processing. A variable declared inside the trigger body resets on every run.

stem: A before-save flow sets Priority to High on a Case. A before trigger on the same object then reads Trigger.new[0].Priority. What does it see?

options.text: High, because before-save flows run before before triggers
The old value, because flows run last
Null, because flows never change fields
It depends on the user's profile

explanation: Before-save flows run first in the order of execution, so the trigger sees the value the flow set.

stem: A validation rule requires Region__c to be filled. A before insert trigger fills Region__c when it is blank. A user saves a record with the field blank. What happens?

options.text: The save succeeds, because the before trigger runs before validation rules
The save fails with the validation message
The save succeeds only for admins

explanation: Before triggers run before custom validation, so the trigger can supply the value and the rule then passes.

stem: Which TWO statements about a before insert trigger are true? (Choose 2)

options.text: Trigger.new fields can be changed without DML
The records do not have Ids yet

explanation: Records are not yet saved, so changes need no DML and there are no Ids. There is no Trigger.old on insert, and newMap needs Ids.
